cause: The validators hold their own method->params tables and kwargs/args rules that drifted from the cores: integers.dtype (no core takes it), a distincts_external entry (no engine maps it), a mandatory kwargs key the pandas generator never required and the Spark generator indexed blindly, legacy args accepted by Spark validation but never passed by get_df, and an ignored NPCore.gen_uuid4 length.
evidence_loop: pytest tests/test_1_common_validator.py tests/test_1_advanced_validator.py: RED 7 failed/61 passed before the fix; GREEN 69 passed; full suite 512 passed
expected: A spec the validator accepts runs on the engine, and a spec the engine runs (including the validator's own examples) validates; one source of truth for method params.
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from rand_engine import DataGenerator as G; G({"a":{"method":"integers","kwargs":{"min":1,"max":5,"dtype":"int"}}}).size(2).get_df()' -> ColumnGenerationError: gen_ints() got an unexpected keyword argument 'dtype'
solution: Deleted the drift instead of deriving params from inspect.signature (pandas and Spark core signatures differ, Spark advanced dummies take **kwargs, and types/examples must stay in the table, so derivation would add an engine switch and special cases): dropped dtype and its messages, the distincts_external entry and checks, the requires-kwargs-or-args rule (absent kwargs = {} on both generators; required params still reported), Spark args now rejected per docs/2_SPARK_GENERATOR.md (kwargs only), validators receive the column config directly, NPCore.gen_uuid4 lost length (SPEC D20). Known residual: legacy pandas args:[n] on uuid4 now passes validation and fails at generation; root cause = the pandas args validation bypass, proposed separately.
symptom: The validator keeps its own method/param tables independent of the cores: it accepts integers.dtype (NPCore raises ColumnGenerationError: unexpected keyword 'dtype'), accepts distincts_external (no engine maps it: KeyError 'distincts_external'), rejects its own uuid4 example without kwargs (pandas and Spark), and NPCore.gen_uuid4 takes a length it ignores.
title: Validator parameter tables drift from the engine method signatures

cause: cast(rand()*(max-min)+min) never reaches max and truncates toward zero for negative ranges
expected: Both engines treat integers max identically (inclusive, as the pandas engine does).
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, functions as F; from rand_engine.main.spark_generator import SparkGenerator; s=SparkSession.builder.master("local[1]").getOrCreate(); print(sorted(r[0] for r in SparkGenerator(s,F,{"a":{"method":"integers","kwargs":{"min":0,"max":1}}}).size(20000).get_df().select("a").distinct().collect()))' -> [0]
solution: floor(rand()*(max-min+1)+min) then cast: inclusive on both ends, matching NPCore
symptom: SparkCore.gen_ints casts rand()*(max-min)+min, so max is exclusive; NPCore uses randint(min, max+1), inclusive. min=0 max=1 on Spark yields only 0.
title: Spark integers never reaches max while pandas includes it

cause: The NumPy engine had two method maps (RandGenerator.map_methods and PyCore's template map, which lacked dates/distincts_prop), the pandas validator skipped every column carrying positional args, and complex_distincts templates bypassed the parameter tables; nothing pinned the validator tables to the engine maps or the callables' signatures
evidence_loop: pytest tests/test_1_advanced_validator.py -k 'args_is_refused or template': RED 7 failed on c040954 (args validated; dtype/missing-min/distincts_map templates validated; dates/distincts_prop templates KeyError) -> GREEN; full suite 686 passed
expected: One contract test pins every validator table against each engine map and callable signature so drift fails CI; PyCore's own template map deleted in favour of the engine's; pandas args removed from the grammar (pk/fk kwargs-only; 0.7.0 allows breaks).
lineage_reason: validator-engine-schema-drift (01ffb21) removed table drift but deliberately kept tables over signature derivation and left the pandas args bypass as a known residual; date-format-required-but-docs-omit-it and advanced-rand-specs-fail-validation fixed drift instances; no prior fix introduced this, the second and third owners (PyCore template map, args grammar) predate them
repro: python -c "from rand_engine import DataGenerator; DataGenerator({'x':{'method':'integers','args':[1]}}).size(2).get_df()"  # validates, then ColumnGenerationError
solution: One NumPy method map (core/_py_core.METHODS) used by RandGenerator and by complex_distincts templates; PyCore's own map and the args generation branch deleted; args refused at validation (Spark already refused it); string templates validated through CommonValidator.METHOD_SPECS, multi-column methods refused; fk's own args check deleted (subsumed); one contract test pins both validator tables to both engine maps and to each callable's parameter names and required set
symptom: Breaks constitution invariant 3 (a spec that validates generates). Five owners drift: CommonValidator.METHOD_SPECS (validators/common_validator.py), AdvancedValidator.METHOD_SPECS (validators/advanced_validator.py), RandGenerator.map_methods (main/_rand_generator.py), SparkGenerator.map_methods (main/spark_generator.py), PyCore's own template map (core/_py_core.py:18-27). (a) pandas args skip validation: {'x':{'method':'integers','args':[1]}} validates then ColumnGenerationError (gen_ints missing positional); uuid4 args:[5] validates then ColumnGenerationError. (b) complex_distincts templates are never parameter-checked: template integers+dtype validates then ColumnGenerationError (unexpected kwarg dtype); template dates validates then KeyError 'dates' (PyCore map lacks dates/distincts_prop).
title: Method set and params live in five places (two validator tables, two engine maps, PyCore template map) and drift

cause: rc-9 J2.T2 added a transitional feature/0.8.0 preview deploy path and a deploy-job eligibility recheck; the environment rule was removed after stable 0.8.0 shipped while the workflow gates and docs_site.py preview code stayed, so GitHub rejected the deploy job before the recheck step ran.
expected: A push to the work branch ends the Docs workflow green with no deploy attempt from that branch (Build Docs only); only master deploys Pages. Contract: deployment_eligibility returns the exact deploy mode or an explained successful skip.
repro: gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/check-runs/$(gh run view 39250886215 --repo <owner>/<repo> --json jobs --jq '.jobs[]|select(.conclusion=="failure")|.databaseId')/annotations --jq '.[].message'  # prints the environment protection message
solution: REBUILD: deleted the preview path and the recheck step as one unit (docs.yml feature/0.8.0 gates and mode switch, PREVIEW_REF, preview prepare mode, remote reads, DeploymentEligibility, check_deployment, write_github_output, deployment-eligibility CLI); the deploy job if (push to master) is the one decider, pinned by test_docs_workflow_deploys_pages_from_master_only.
symptom: Docs run 39250886215 (push of 3c6c73d to feature/0.8.0): Build Docs succeeds, Deploy Pages fails with 'Branch "feature/0.8.0" is not allowed to deploy to github-pages due to environment protection rules.' The deploy job admits refs/heads/feature/0.8.0 (if: line 63) and declares environment github-pages (line 66); GitHub evaluates the environment branch policy before any step, so deployment-eligibility (scripts/docs_site.py:139, which would return skip because master is no longer 0.7.0) never runs. The preview path (PREVIEW_REF, preview mode, 0.8.0/0.7.0 version pins) is a transitional pre-release path dead since stable 0.8.0 shipped. Introduced by rc-9 J2.T2 (commit 22f1d66).
title: Docs deploy job fails on feature/0.8.0 push: environment protection rejects the branch before the eligibility step runs
